chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Playing proms and schools for white audiences around Buffalo
summary: Crawford says the band played proms and colleges, stayed in private colored homes, and played the same book everywhere.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: -- you don't -- now, did you consider Lunsford -- you don't -- did you consider the Lunsford band a society band? You -- in Cleveland?
We were trying to be all that because we played a lot of proms, commencements and different big schools.
Even in Cleveland in, you know, when
We played a few proms and odd jobs, but when we were in Buffalo, we played quite a number of big schools, Cornell, University of Rochester and schools of that --
Now, were you playing -- when you played those schools, were you playing -- you were playing for, mostly for white, for white audiences, right?
Well, it was a little mixed, but mostly white.
Mostly white. Now, did you -- when you all went to play those jobs, did you -- did you live near or on the campus or did you come there like in a bus?
No, we'd stay in different homes, private homes, colored.
How did you meet the people that you stayed with in those days?
Oh, fine.
I mean how did you meet them? I mean like --
Oh, Lunsford got us the rooms.
The people -- he would know the people through different contacts?
Well, not necessarily -- yeah, through contacts. Also we were staying at Mom's place, which
fed us also. We had to pay for it. She had a dining room, she cooked barbecued ribs, all those kind of things, neck bones, black-eyed peas and et cetera.
So now, when you all weren't staying in colored hotels, you stayed in private homes?
Yes. Yes.
And so now, in those days people didn't -- people weren't -- they didn't have a bad attitude about musicians then?
No. Maybe they did, but we never knew. I didn't, (For one, know.) They were very hospitable and nice, very nice.
And so now like did you play at different -- did you all play, have a different repertoire for like the proms and commencements than you did --
No, same thing.
Night clubs and proms, you played the material.
Yeah, high society and a mixture of -- oh, we were -- maybe they considered us to be a society colored group, but we played just what we had in the book, that's all.
